question: What is the tenure of the President of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India is elected for a term of **5 years** according to Article 56 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The election process for the President is outlined in Article 54 and Article 55 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The term of the President can be extended if the elections are not completed before the expiry of the term, as per Article 56(1)(c).
 
• A President can be re-elected and there is no limit on the number of terms a person can serve as President.
 
• The President continues to hold office until his successor is duly elected and enters office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Procedure:**

 
 
• The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both houses of Parliament as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The voting is done by secret ballot using the single transferable vote system.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• A candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• He/she should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India, a state government, or any public authority.
 
 
 
• **Impeachment:**
 
 
• The President can be removed from office through a process called impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
 
• The impeachment process can be initiated in either House of Parliament and requires a two-thirds majority in both houses.
 
 
 
• **Oath of Office:**
 
 
• The President takes an oath or affirmation before entering upon the office, which is administered by the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available.
